source_text: κατὰ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ, δυνάμει κραταιωθῆναι διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρω πον κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστόν.» 5.18 ἐκλάβοιμεν δ' ἂν ἐν ὁμοίῳ καὶ ἴσῳ τό· «ἐγένετο λόγος κυρίου πρὸς τόνδε τὸν προφήτην» καὶ τό· «κύριος εἶπεν» καί· «τάδε λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ» τῷ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσιν ὑπὸ Πέτρου εἰρημένῳ· «ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν γραφήν, ἣν προεῖπεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον» καὶ τῷ ὑπὸ Παύλου ἐν Ῥώμῃ πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· «καλῶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐλάλησεν διὰ Ἠσαίου τοῦ προφή του» καὶ τῷ· «τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ῥητῶς λέγει» καί· «τάδε λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ». 5.19 ἰσότιμόν τε τῷ· «ὁ θεὸς αἰώνιος» τὸ ὑπὸ Παύλου κηρυχθέν· «ὃς ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου.» συγκριτικόν τε τῷ· «οὐδεὶς δύναται πνεῦμα ἅγιον λαβεῖν ἢ παρὰ κυρίου» καὶ τῷ· «λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον» τό· «οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, εἰ μὴ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.» 5.20 ταὐτόν τέ ἐστιν τό· «ὁδηγεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν,» τουτέστιν τὸ ὁδηγεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος πρὸς τὴν ἀληθινὴν πίστιν, τῷ ὁδηγεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ δεσπότου Χριστοῦ θεσπίζοντος· «βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος.» καὶ ἰσοσθενὲς τῷ λέγοντι ῥητῷ· «μὴ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον; μὴ ἰσχυρότεροι αὐτοῦ ἐσμεν;» τὸ γράφειν· «μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως.» καὶ ὁμοιόλεκτον τῷ· «ἐξαποστελεῖς τὸ πνεῦμά σου καὶ κτισθήσονται» τό· «ἐξαποστελεῖς τὸν λόγον σου, καὶ τήξει αὐτά.» 5.21 ἰσάμιλλόν τε τῷ εἰπεῖν· «κύριος μαρτυρεῖ τῇ ἐμῇ ψυχῇ, ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι» τὸ γράφειν· «τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὃ παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται, ἐκεῖ νος μαρτυρήσει περὶ ἐμοῦ·» καί· 53 «τὸ πνεῦμα διαμαρτύρεταί με κατὰ πόλιν λέγον.» ἀπεικασμένον τε τῷ λέγοντι δεσποτικῷ ῥήματι· «ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς, ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων,» τό· «οὗτοι μὲν οὖν ἐκπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, κατῆλθον εἰς Σελεύκειαν.» 5.22 καὶ ἴσον τὸ γράφειν· «εἰ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοῖ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ», τῷ γράφειν, ὅτι· «ἔλεγον τῷ Παύλῳ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος· μὴ ἀνάβαινε εἰς Ἰερου σαλήμ.» συγγενές τε τῷ· «ὁ υἱὸς ζωὴ αἰώνιος» τὸ ὑπὸ αὐτοῦ λεχθέν· «τὸ ὕδωρ, ὃ ἐγὼ δώσω αὐτῷ, γενήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἁλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύοντες εἰς αὐτόν,» καὶ τῷ· «μέτοχοι γὰρ τοῦ Χριστοῦ γεγόναμεν» τό· «ἀδύνατον γὰρ τοὺς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας γευσαμένους τε τῆς δωρεᾶς τοῦ ἐπουρανίου, καὶ μετόχους γενηθέντας πνεύματος ἁγίου.» 5.23 καὶ ἔοικεν σφόδρα τὸ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι τοιῶσδε εἰρημένον· 5.23 «ὤφθησαν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐφ' ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπλήθησαν ἅπαντες πνεύματος ἁγίου», καὶ τὸ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου λεχθέν· «αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί» τῷ χρησμῳδηθέντι ὑπὸ μὲν Μωυσέως· «ὁ θεὸς πῦρ καταναλίσκον·» ὑπὸ δὲ Ἠσαίου· «ἰδοὺ κύριος ὡς πῦρ ἥξει.» καὶ συνᾴδει τῷ φάναι· «περιετμήθητε περιτομῇ ἀχειροποιήτῳ, ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τοῦ σώ ματος τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἐν τῇ περιτομῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ» τὸ γεγράφθαι· «περιτομὴ καρδίας ἐν πνεύματι.» 5.24 καὶ εἰ ἐμπρέπει περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγεσθαι τὴν Πέτρου φωνήν· «μετανοήσει ἕκαστος ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὁδοῦ τῆς πονηρᾶς καὶ βαπτισθήτω εἰς τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, καὶ σω θήσεται·» ἄρα τῷ θεῷ ἀπαράλλακτον τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ τὸν δεσπότην τοῖς μαθηταῖς, αὐτοῖς ὀνόμασι φάναι· «ἀναμείνατε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρός, ἣν ἠκούσατε, ὅτι Ἰω άννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν, ὑμεῖς δὲ βαπτισθή σεσθε ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίου.» οὐδὲν γὰρ ἕτερον τοῦτο δηλοῖ, ἢ ὅπερ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη αὐτοῦ περὶ τὸ φώτισμα μυσταγωγία, ὅτι δὴ τὰ αὐτὰ ἐνεργεῖ καὶ δύναται τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, ἅπερ τοὔνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ, ἅτε τῆς αὐτῆς ὑπάρχον θεότητος. 5.25 ἀπαράλλακτόν τε τὸ κήρυγμα τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος καὶ ἐξ ἴσου σεπτόν, ᾗ Παῦλος Ῥωμαίοις γράφει· «εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει, ὃν οὐκ ἐκη ρύξαμεν, ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε, ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε.» τὴν αὐτὴν ἔνδειξιν ἔχει καὶ τό· «οὐ γὰρ τολμῶ τι λαλεῖν, ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο Χριστὸς δι' ἐμοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τερά των, ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος θεοῦ,» τῷ· «ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων, αὐτὸς ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα. πιστεύετε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί.» 5.26 παρατήρει γάρ, ὅτιπερ ὡς ὁ πατήρ, οὕτως καὶ τὸ

And comparable with 'no one can receive Holy Spirit except from the Lord' and with 'receive Holy Spirit' [is] 'no one can say Lord Jesus Christ except in Holy Spirit'. 5.20 And the same is 'to be guided by the Holy Spirit to the truth', that is, to be guided by the Holy Spirit to the true faith, as being guided by the Master Christ decreeing: 'baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit'. pass_b_english: …according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit, so that Christ may dwell in the inner man” (Ephesians 3:16–17).

We may take as alike and equal “The word of the Lord came to such and such a prophet,” and “The Lord said,” and “Thus says the Lord Almighty,” with what Peter said in the Acts, “The Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand” (Acts 1:16); with what Paul said in Rome to the Jews, “Well did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet” (Acts 28:25); and with “But the Spirit expressly says” (1 Timothy 4:1), and “Thus says the Lord Almighty.”

Of equal honour with “the eternal God” is what Paul proclaimed: “who offered himself through the eternal Spirit” (Hebrews 9:14). Comparable with “No one can receive the Holy Spirit except from the Lord,” and with “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22), is “No one can say ‘Lord Jesus Christ’ except in the Holy Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:3).

To be “guided by the Holy Spirit into the truth” (John 16:13), that is, to be guided by the Holy Spirit into the true faith, is the same as to be guided by the Master Christ when he decrees, “baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19). Of equal strength with the text that says, “Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?” (1 Corinthians 10:22), is the writing, “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption” (Ephesians 4:30). And worded alike with “You will send forth your Spirit, and they will be created” (Psalm 104:30) is “You will send forth your word, and it will melt them” (Psalm 147:18).

On a par with saying, “The Lord bears witness to my soul that I do not lie,” is the writing, “The Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me” (John 15:26), and “The Spirit bears witness to me in every city, saying” (Acts 20:23). And likened to the Master’s saying, “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves” (Matthew 10:16), is “So these, sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia” (Acts 13:4).

The writing “Since you seek proof of the Christ who speaks in me” (2 Corinthians 13:3) is equal to the writing that “they told Paul through the Spirit, Do not go up to Jerusalem” (Acts 21:4). Akin to “The Son is eternal life” is what he himself said: “The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up to eternal life” (John 4:14). “Now this he said about the Holy Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive” (John 7:39). And akin to “For we have become partakers of Christ” (Hebrews 3:14) is “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and become partakers of the Holy Spirit” (Hebrews 6:4).

What is said in the Acts in these words, “There appeared to the apostles tongues as of fire, divided, and they sat on each one of them, and all were filled with the Holy Spirit” (Acts 2:3–4), and what John said, “He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire” (Matthew 3:11), are very like what was declared by Moses, “God is a consuming fire” (Deuteronomy 4:24), and by Isaiah, “Behold, the Lord will come as fire” (Isaiah 66:15). And the saying “You were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in putting off the body of sins, in the circumcision of Christ” (Colossians 2:11) is in harmony with the written words “circumcision of the heart, in the Spirit” (Romans 2:29).

And if Peter’s words are fitly said about God, “Let each one repent of his wickedness and of the evil way, and be baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, and he will be saved” (Acts 2:38), then his Spirit is indistinguishable from God. This is plain also from the Master’s words to the disciples, in so many words: “Wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard, that John baptized with water for repentance, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit” (Acts 1:4–5). For this shows nothing other than what his other teaching on the rite of enlightenment shows: that the Holy Spirit works and is able to do the very things that the name of the Father and of his Son does, since he is of the same Godhead.

The preaching of the Son and that of the Holy Spirit are without difference and equally to be revered, as Paul writes to the Romans: “For if he who comes preaches another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit, which you did not receive” (2 Corinthians 11:4). The same proof lies in “For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has worked through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God” (Romans 15:18–19), as in “The Father who abides in me does the works himself. Believe that I am in the Father and the Father in me” (John 14:10–11). For observe that, as the Father, so too the …

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft; comparisons broken; references missing or abbreviated
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u13): retranslated from the Greek. Didymus pairs a text about the Father or the Son with a text about the Spirit ('X is equal to Y'); the old English turned several pairs into flat lists ('it is comparative to ... and to ... and to'), rendered τήξει 'it shall establish them' (melt), σώματος 'flesh', ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι 'in the actions', ἀπαράλλακτον 'likewise unchanging', and 'the same things, which is the name of the Father' (the same things that the name of the Father does); it split the John 4:14 quotation across two paragraphs and opened with the bracket '[he is]'. References: (1 Cor 12:3), (Matt 28:19), (Eph 4:30), (Matt 10:16) written out; (John 4:14) kept and John 7:39 added for the second half of the quotation. Added: Ephesians 3:16–17, 1 Timothy 4:1, John 20:22, John 16:13, Psalm 104:30, Psalm 147:18, Acts 20:23, Acts 13:4, 2 Corinthians 13:3, Hebrews 3:14, Hebrews 6:4, Acts 2:3–4, Matthew 3:11, Deuteronomy 4:24, Isaiah 66:15, Colossians 2:11, Romans 2:29, Acts 2:38, Acts 1:4–5, 2 Corinthians 11:4, Romans 15:18–19, John 14:10–11.

choices.english: …according to the riches of his glory … (Ephesians 3:16–17)
choices.why: The quotation begins in the previous section ('that he may grant you'); only the words this section holds are translated, opened with '…', and the reference is placed where the quotation ends.

choices.term: εἰς τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστόν
choices.english: so that Christ may dwell in the inner man
choices.why: Didymus compresses Ephesians 3:16–17 ('in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts'); the English keeps his shorter form.

choices.english: to such and such a prophet
choices.why: τόνδε stands for any prophet's name in the stock formula.

The copy-text repeats the Old Testament formula at the end of the list of Spirit texts, where the sense calls for a saying of the Spirit (Acts 21:11, 'Thus says the Holy Spirit'); translated as it stands and flagged in problems.

choices.term: συγκριτικόν τε τῷ ... καὶ τῷ ... τό
choices.why: Two texts on the side of the Lord are matched with one text about the Spirit; the old English made all three a list.

choices.term: «ἐξαποστελεῖς τὸν λόγον σου, καὶ τήξει αὐτά»
choices.english: “You will send forth your word, and it will melt them” (Psalm 147:18)
choices.why: Psalm 147:7 in the Greek numbering (147:18 English) reads 'he will send out his word and melt them'; Didymus puts it in the second person to match Psalm 104:30, and his wording is kept.
53 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.

choices.term: ἐκεῖ νος, Ἰερου σαλήμ, προφή του, ἄνθρω πον, σώ ματος, σω θήσεται, Ἰω άννης, βαπτισθή σεσθε, ἐκη ρύξαμεν, τερά των
choices.why: Words split by the copy-text's line breaks; read whole.
The edition number 5.23 is printed a second time inside the sentence in the copy-text; debris.

choices.english: What is said in the Acts … and what John said … are very like what was declared by Moses … and by Isaiah
choices.why: Two fire texts about the Spirit are matched with two fire texts about God.
Didymus names Moses; Deuteronomy 4:24 has the words (also 9:3, and Hebrews 12:29 quoting them).

choices.term: «μετανοήσει ἕκαστος ... βαπτισθήτω εἰς τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου Ἰησοῦ»
choices.english: “Let each one repent … and be baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, and he will be saved” (Acts 2:38)
choices.why: Peter's call in Acts 2:38, which Didymus enlarges with prophetic wording ('from the evil way', as in Jonah 3:8) and 'he will be saved' (Acts 2:21); μετανοήσει (future) is read as a command beside βαπτισθήτω.
'In the very words': the Master's own saying, quoted exactly.
The genitive ἁγίου is a slip for ἁγίῳ (Acts 1:5).

choices.term: ἡ ἄλλη αὐτοῦ περὶ τὸ φώτισμα μυσταγωγία
choices.english: his other teaching on the rite of enlightenment
choices.why: φώτισμα, 'enlightenment', is baptism; the 'other teaching' is the baptismal command of Matthew 28:19 quoted in 5.20.

choices.term: ἅπερ τοὔνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ
choices.english: the very things that the name of the Father and of his Son does
choices.why: The verbs carry over: the Spirit does what the name of Father and Son does in baptism. παῖς rendered 'Son' (as in Acts 4:27, 30).

choices.english: as Paul writes to the Romans
choices.why: The quoted verse is 2 Corinthians 11:4, not Romans; Didymus' (or the copyist's) attribution is kept and the correct verse cited. See problems.

choices.term: παρατήρει γάρ, ὅτιπερ ὡς ὁ πατήρ, οὕτως καὶ τὸ
choices.english: For observe that, as the Father, so too the …
choices.why: The sentence runs into the next section ('his Spirit abides with Christ'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
